An agent does not arrive at a task knowing nothing. It arrives carrying
directives, memories, a record of how this person wants to be asked, and
whatever confirmations were granted in advance. All of that is **context**: it
shapes how a process runs without being part of what the process produces.

A **Context Overlay** is a set of that material applied deliberately, so the
same workflow can be run again under the same conditions — or run twice under
deliberately different ones, and the difference attributed to the context
rather than to chance.

**"Overlay" means three unrelated things in this documentation**, so the Term
on this page is **Context Overlay** and not the bare word.

| where | what it means |
|---|---|
| this page | a set of context material applied to a run |
| [`getting-started`](../start/getting-started.html) §6 | a BRANCH of the folio-intent gateway — converting a repository you already have |
| [`getting-started`](../start/getting-started.html) §8 | positioning text ON cat artwork, where an undeclared region means "do not overlay" |

A reader who carries the bare word's meaning from one section into another is
misled in a way that is hard to notice, because every sentence still parses.
So: **Context Overlay** when this page's sense is meant. Where the other two
are meant, name them — the gateway branch, or the art region.

## What a Context Overlay is
{: #what-a-context-overlay-is data-fa-label="sec:managing-agent-context-what-a-context-overlay-is" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/what-a-context-overlay-is.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/what-a-context-overlay-is.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/what-a-context-overlay-is.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="what-a-context-overlay-is.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/what-a-context-overlay-is.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="what-a-context-overlay-is.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/what-a-context-overlay-is.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

Context is generated in several different ways, and the point of the Term is
that they compose. A Context Overlay MAY be assembled from any of them:

- **Agent directives** — the instruction files an agent reads on arrival.
- **Memory** — durable facts an agent carries between sessions.
- **Interaction preferences** — how this person wants to be asked.
- **Waivers** — confirmations granted in advance, each naming one gate.
- **Methodologies** — an adopted way of reaching a judgement.

What makes them one kind of thing is not their format. It is their relation to
a running process:

> **Context is READ during a process and never written by one.**

The graph layer checks it. A step that writes to a Context graph is a defect, not an
update — which is exactly what makes an overlay reproducible: if a run could
modify its own context, the second run would not be the same experiment.

## What the Context layer holds
{: #the-context-layer data-fa-label="sec:managing-agent-context-the-context-layer" }

The Context layer is declared, not inferred. Five graph typologies currently sit in
it, and the schema requires each kind to say which layer it belongs to, so a
kind that has not decided does not compile:

| kind | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `memory` | durable facts an agent carries between sessions |
| `interaction` | how a person wants to be asked — read at session start |
| `waiver` | confirmations granted in advance, each naming one gate |
| `methodology` | an adopted way of reaching a judgement, kept whole |
| `fsh-guts` | deprecated and throwaway structured content, kept addressable |

Ask the code rather than this table — `graphTypologiesOfLayer("context")` returns
the live answer; a count written into prose is not re-derived.
The shapes are in
[`schemas/cat-harness.ts`](https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/blob/main/cat-harness/schemas/cat-harness.ts).

`fsh-guts` holds
structured material that COULD be rendered, which is what makes it look like
content. It is context because no running process writes it.

## Why overlaying makes a test repeatable
{: #why-repeatable data-fa-label="sec:managing-agent-context-why-repeatable" }

[✎ Edit](https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness/edit/main/docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/why-repeatable.md){: .fa-node-edit title="Edit docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/why-repeatable.md" data-fa-link="edit" data-src="docs/source/guides-managing-agent-context/why-repeatable.md" data-repo="litlfred/cat-harness" } <span class="fa-qa-badges"><button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-block" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="block" data-qa-key="why-repeatable.block" data-qa-label="Content QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/why-repeatable.block.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Content QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Content QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">QA</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button> <button type="button" class="fa-qa-badge fa-qa-pending fa-qa-fam-translation" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-qa-family="translation" data-qa-key="why-repeatable.translation" data-qa-label="Translation QA" data-qa-noun="block" data-qa-src="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/why-repeatable.translation.json' | relative_url }}" data-qa-index="{{ '/assets/qa/guides-managing-agent-context/qa-index.json' | relative_url }}" aria-expanded="false" aria-busy="true" title="Translation QA: loading the verdict…" aria-label="Translation QA: loading the verdict…"><span class="fa-qa-tag">TR</span><span class="fa-qa-glyph" aria-hidden="true">…</span></button></span>

The reason to name this at all is testing.

If context is ambient — whatever happened to be in the environment when the
run started — then two runs of the same workflow are not comparable, and a
difference in outcome cannot be attributed. Was it the model? The prompt? A
memory entry one session wrote and another did not have?

Overlaying context makes that question answerable. The workflow is held fixed,
the Context Overlay is stated, and a difference between runs is a difference
between overlays. It is the same move as pinning a dependency version, because
an unpinned one makes every other measurement unreliable.

This is what lets the repository ask how models compare across sub-workflows
**under a controlled overlay of context and memories** — a question named as
open research in [`agentic-harness`](../concepts/agentic-harness.html), not as something
settled here.

This page explains the concept. The discipline is in the skills, and where the
two disagree the skill wins:

- [`agent-memory`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/agent-memory.html' | relative_url }}) — the three
  entry labels, why entries are authored as nodes rather than in the generated
  file, and the injection budget.
- [`content-context-and-state-graphs`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/content-context-and-state-graphs.html' | relative_url }})
  — the one question that settles a layer, and why a step writing to a Context
  graph is a defect.
- [`confirmation-waiver`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/confirmation-waiver.html' | relative_url }})
  — a confirmation granted in advance, scoped to a session or a process run.
- [`interaction-modality`]({{ '/reference/skill-instructions/interaction-modality.html' | relative_url }})
  — how a person wants to be asked.

Setting an agent's context deterministically from the knowledge graph at each
task is not yet built. It is said here because a page that described it as
working would read exactly like one that described something real.
